answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may earn reputation or claim work. If an identity is caught double-claiming or coordinating fraud, an auditable challenge process slashes that deposit; otherwise it remains locked and earns no return. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund every persona and risk losing capital, so fabricating identities at scale becomes costly. A harbor might call its reward nectar and its public ledger crystal-clear, but the deterrent is the bond at stake.
